**`wehoop` is an R package for women's basketball data: the WNBA, NCAA
women's college basketball, and a growing list of women's leagues and national
team competitions around the world.** It gives you two ways in. Release loaders
(`load_*()`) download whole seasons of pre-built play-by-play, box scores and
model outputs in seconds. Live wrappers (`espn_*()`, `wnba_*()`, and the
international families) call a source directly when you need today's game or a
dataset nobody has pre-built.

This guide is for students and newcomers. It assumes no prior experience with
sports data and only a little R.

## What you'll learn

- How to install `wehoop` and the packages used in this guide.
- How the function names map to data sources, so you can guess the function you
  need.
- How to load a full WNBA season of team box scores and play-by-play.
- How to turn a box score into a team statistic and draw your first chart with
  `ggplot2`.
- The basketball analytics vocabulary (possessions, pace, ratings, true shooting
  and the rest) used across the other articles.
- Where to go next.

## How do I install wehoop?

`wehoop` needs R 4.1.0 or newer. If you are starting from zero, install R from
[CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org) and then the free
[RStudio Desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) editor. Windows
users should also install [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/),
which R uses to build packages from source.

Then install the package. The CRAN release is the stable choice. The GitHub
version gets new data sources first.

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
# CRAN release
install.packages("wehoop")

# Development version from GitHub
if (!requireNamespace("pak", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("sportsdataverse/wehoop")

# Packages used in the examples below
install.packages(c("dplyr", "ggplot2", "tidyr"))
```

A few loaders read Apache Parquet files. They need the `arrow` package
(`install.packages("arrow")`). The functions that fit a RAPM model need
`glmnet` and `Matrix`.

```{r libraries}
library(wehoop)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Which function reads which source?

The prefix of a function name tells you where its data comes from. Learn the
prefixes and the rest of the package becomes guessable: `espn_wnba_pbp()` and
`espn_wbb_pbp()` take the same arguments and return the same columns, one for
the WNBA and one for women's college basketball.

| Prefix | Source | What you get | Network call? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `load_wnba_*()` | sportsdataverse GitHub releases (ESPN-derived) | Whole WNBA seasons: play-by-play, team and player box scores, schedules, rosters, shots, officials | Downloads a pre-built file |
| `load_wbb_*()` | sportsdataverse GitHub releases (ESPN-derived) | The same tables for NCAA women's college basketball, plus `load_wbb_ratings()` and `load_wbb_player_value()` | Downloads a pre-built file |
| `load_wnba_stats_*()` | sportsdataverse GitHub releases (WNBA Stats API-derived) | WNBA Stats schedules, play-by-play, shots, lineups, league dashboards, possessions | Downloads a pre-built file |
| `load_ncaa_wbb_*()` | sportsdataverse GitHub releases (stats.ncaa.org-derived) | NCAA play-by-play, shots, lineups, stints, possessions, RAPM | Downloads a pre-built file |
| `espn_wnba_*()`, `espn_wbb_*()` | ESPN site and core APIs | Live scoreboards, games, rosters, athletes, standings, odds, news | Yes |
| `wnba_*()` | WNBA Stats API (stats.wnba.com) | Deep WNBA stats: league dashboards, hustle, tracking, lineups, shot charts | Yes |
| `ncaa_wbb_*()` | NCAA.com | NET rankings and the team list | Yes |
| `fox_*()` | Fox Sports | WNBA and WBB scores, box scores, play-by-play | Yes |
| `bref_wnba_*()`, `hhs_*()`, `bart_wbb_*()` | Basketball-Reference, Her Hoop Stats (subscription), Bart Torvik | Season tables and ratings | Yes |
| `fiba_*()`, `genius_*()`, `atrium_*()`, `nbl_rosetta_*()`, `scb_*()`, `feb_*()`, `tbf_*()`, `wjbl_*()`, `wbbl_*()`, `lfb_*()`, ... | International league and federation feeds | Women's World Cup, Olympics, EuroLeague Women, WNBL, W League and more | Yes |

The full list, grouped by family, is the [function reference](../reference/index.html).
Jump straight to a group:

### Release loaders or live wrappers?

Reach for a `load_*()` function whenever you want history. It reads one file per
season from a public GitHub release, so a full season arrives in seconds and you
never hit a rate limit. Every loader takes a `seasons` argument: a single year, a
vector such as `2022:2025`, or `TRUE` for every published season.

Reach for a live wrapper when you need a game that finished an hour ago, or a
dataset that is not pre-built. Live wrappers are slower, and the sources behind
them can throttle you if you loop over hundreds of requests.

A season is labelled by the calendar year for the WNBA (`2025` is the 2025
season) and by the **ending** year for college (`2026` is the 2025-26 season).
`most_recent_wnba_season()` and `most_recent_wbb_season()` return the current
label.

## A first worked example: a WNBA season in five minutes

This guide uses the 2025 WNBA season, the most recent one with a full regular
season and playoffs at the time of writing.

```{r season}
wnba_season <- 2025
```

### Load the team box scores

`load_wnba_team_box()` returns one row per team per game.

```{r team-box}
team_box <- load_wnba_team_box(seasons = wnba_season)

dim(team_box)

team_box |>
  select(game_date, team_abbreviation, team_score,
         opponent_team_abbreviation, opponent_team_score, season_type) |>
  head()
```

`season_type` is `2` for the regular season and `3` for the playoffs. Each game
appears twice, once from each team's side, which is why `opponent_*` columns sit
next to the team's own. The release covers `r length(unique(team_box$game_id))`
games for `r wnba_season`.

### Compute a team statistic

Raw points per game mixes two things: how efficient a team is, and how many
chances it gets. Analysts separate them by counting **possessions**, the number
of times a team has the ball. A box score does not record possessions directly,
so we estimate them from field goal attempts, offensive rebounds, turnovers and
free throw attempts (the formula is in the [glossary](#glossary)). Points per
100 possessions is called **offensive rating**.

```{r team-ratings}
team_ratings <- team_box |>
  filter(season_type == 2) |>
  mutate(
    possessions = field_goals_attempted - offensive_rebounds +
      turnovers + 0.44 * free_throws_attempted
  ) |>
  group_by(team_abbreviation) |>
  summarise(
    games = n(),
    points = sum(team_score),
    points_allowed = sum(opponent_team_score),
    possessions = sum(possessions),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  # The All-Star Game is filed as a regular-season game between two
  # one-off "teams"; keep only the real franchises.
  filter(games >= 20) |>
  mutate(
    off_rating = 100 * points / possessions,
    def_rating = 100 * points_allowed / possessions,
    net_rating = off_rating - def_rating
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(net_rating))

team_ratings
```

(We use the team's own possessions as the denominator for both ratings. Both
teams have nearly the same number of possessions in a game, so the difference is
small. The [advanced metrics article](womens-basketball-advanced-metrics.html)
covers the refinements.)

### Draw your first chart

```{r first-plot, fig.alt = "Scatter plot of 2025 WNBA teams: offensive rating on the x-axis and defensive rating on the y-axis, with the y-axis reversed so better defenses sit higher."}
ggplot(team_ratings, aes(off_rating, def_rating)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(team_ratings$def_rating), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(team_ratings$off_rating), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#221A4D") +
  geom_text(aes(label = team_abbreviation), vjust = -0.9, size = 3.5) +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  labs(
    title = paste(wnba_season, "WNBA regular season: team efficiency"),
    subtitle = "Points scored and allowed per 100 estimated possessions. Up and to the right is better.",
    x = "Offensive rating", y = "Defensive rating (reversed)",
    caption = "Data: wehoop::load_wnba_team_box()"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Teams in the top-right quadrant score efficiently and defend well.

### Load play-by-play

Play-by-play (often shortened to **pbp**) has one row per event: every shot,
rebound, foul, turnover, substitution and timeout, with the clock and score at
that moment.

```{r pbp}
pbp <- load_wnba_pbp(seasons = wnba_season)

nrow(pbp)
length(unique(pbp$game_id))

pbp |>
  select(game_id, period_number, clock_display_value, type_text,
         scoring_play, score_value, home_score, away_score) |>
  head()
```

A quick question pbp can answer and a box score cannot: when in the game do
points get scored?

```{r points-by-period}
pbp |>
  filter(scoring_play == TRUE, period_number <= 4) |>
  group_by(period_number) |>
  summarise(points = sum(score_value), games = n_distinct(game_id), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(points_per_game = points / games)
```

The `pbp` table also carries `game_spread`, `home_favorite`,
`game_spread_available` and `home_team_spread`. In the current releases these
columns hold a placeholder value, not a real market line, so leave them out of
any analysis.

### Load player box scores

```{r player-box}
player_box <- load_wnba_player_box(seasons = wnba_season)

player_box |>
  filter(season_type == 2, did_not_play == FALSE) |>
  group_by(athlete_display_name, team_abbreviation) |>
  summarise(
    games = n(),
    ppg = mean(points, na.rm = TRUE),
    rpg = mean(rebounds, na.rm = TRUE),
    apg = mean(assists, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(games >= 20) |>
  arrange(desc(ppg)) |>
  head(10)
```

### The same code works for college

Swap `wnba` for `wbb` and use a college season label. The tables are larger:
Division I has more than 360 teams and plays several thousand games a season.

```{r wbb-example, eval = FALSE}
wbb_team_box <- load_wbb_team_box(seasons = 2026)
wbb_pbp <- load_wbb_pbp(seasons = 2026)
```

### Live data for a single game

When a game has just finished, the live ESPN wrappers return it straight from
the source. These calls need a network connection, so they are not run here.

```{r live, eval = FALSE}
# Today's WNBA scoreboard
espn_wnba_scoreboard(season = format(Sys.Date(), "%Y%m%d"))

# Play-by-play, team box and player box for one game in a single list
game <- espn_wnba_game_all(game_id = "401736171")
names(game)

# A college team's roster (UConn, ESPN team id 2509)
espn_wbb_team_roster(team_id = 2509, season = 2026)
```

The [ESPN endpoints article](espn-endpoints.html) is a tour of every ESPN
wrapper. The WNBA Stats API wrappers (`wnba_*()`) take more parameters; the
[parameter descriptions](parameter-descriptions.html) table explains each one.

## Glossary {#glossary}

These terms appear throughout the `wehoop` articles. Formulas use box score
abbreviations: FGA field goal attempts, FGM makes, 3PM three-pointers made, FTA
free throw attempts, OREB and DREB offensive and defensive rebounds, TOV
turnovers.

**Possession.** One team's turn with the ball, which ends with a made shot, a
defensive rebound, a turnover or the end of a period. An offensive rebound
continues the same possession. Estimated from a box score as
`FGA - OREB + TOV + 0.44 * FTA`; the 0.44 accounts for free throws that come in
pairs and those that do not end a possession. Play-by-play lets you count
possessions directly, as `load_wnba_stats_possessions()` and
`load_ncaa_wbb_possessions()` do.

**Pace.** Possessions per 40 minutes (both the WNBA and NCAA play 40-minute
games). A faster team creates more possessions, which inflates its per-game
totals.

**Offensive rating (ORtg).** Points scored per 100 possessions.
**Defensive rating (DRtg)** is points allowed per 100 possessions, and
**net rating** is ORtg minus DRtg.

**Effective field goal percentage (eFG%).** `(FGM + 0.5 * 3PM) / FGA`. Gives a
three-pointer 1.5 times the credit of a two.

**True shooting percentage (TS%).** `PTS / (2 * (FGA + 0.44 * FTA))`. Shooting
efficiency including free throws.

**Usage rate.** The share of a team's possessions a player uses (by shooting,
getting to the line, or turning it over) while she is on the court.

**Four factors.** Dean Oliver's four drivers of winning: shooting (eFG%),
turnovers (TOV%), offensive rebounding (OREB%) and getting to the free throw
line (FT rate, `FTA / FGA` or `FTM / FGA`). Each is measured for a team's
offense and its defense.

**Plus/minus.** The point differential while a player is on the court. The
`plus_minus` column in `load_wnba_player_box()` is per game.

**Stint.** A stretch of game time in which the same ten players are on the
court. A substitution ends a stint. `load_ncaa_wbb_matchup_stints()` publishes
them for college.

**Lineup.** The five players one team has on the court. `load_wnba_stats_lineups()`
and `load_ncaa_wbb_lineups()` summarise lineup performance.

**RAPM (regularized adjusted plus-minus).** A regression that estimates each
player's effect on points per 100 possessions while holding the other nine
players fixed. Ridge regularization pulls players with little playing time
toward zero. See the [WNBA player impact](wnba-player-impact-model.html)
and [women's college RAPM](womens-college-basketball-rapm-model.html)
model articles.

**Box plus/minus (BPM).** An estimate of a player's impact per 100 possessions
from box score statistics alone. See the
[player value model](womens-college-basketball-player-value-model.html).

**Win probability (WP).** The chance a team wins from a given game state (score,
time, possession). See the
[win probability model](womens-college-basketball-win-probability-model.html).

**Recipes and tours**

- [WNBA Cookbook](wnba-cookbook.html) and [WBB Cookbook](wbb-cookbook.html):
  short recipes for common questions, league by league.
- [ESPN Endpoints](espn-endpoints.html): every ESPN wrapper, grouped by task.
- [Parameter Descriptions](parameter-descriptions.html): the WNBA Stats API
  query parameters.

**Analysis**

- [Shot charts](wnba-womens-college-basketball-shot-charts.html):
  plot shots on a court, compare makes and misses, and compute field goal
  percentage by zone.
- [Advanced metrics](womens-basketball-advanced-metrics.html):
  possessions, pace, ratings, the four factors, true shooting and usage, with
  every formula shown.
- [International women's basketball](womens-international-basketball-leagues.html):
  which league and competition each international family covers.

**Models**

- [WNBA player impact](wnba-player-impact-model.html): RAPM, SPM, BPM,
  WAR and a DARKO-style projection for every WNBA player-season.
- [Women's college RAPM](womens-college-basketball-rapm-model.html):
  league-wide and within-team RAPM for Division I, plus fitting your own RAPM
  with `wnba_rapm()`.
- [Women's college team ratings](womens-college-basketball-team-ratings-model.html):
  opponent-adjusted offensive and defensive efficiency.
- [Women's college player value](womens-college-basketball-player-value-model.html):
  box plus/minus.
- [Women's college win probability](womens-college-basketball-win-probability-model.html):
  the in-game win probability columns in the play-by-play.
